STAGE 1 - scope scan and what is reachable.
GOAL: find which inputs I can actually inspect, and fix the admissible design space before proposing.
READ: workspace glob of /fs04/.../agents/metric_ideation_5 -> only running.json, session.jsonl, stderr.log, progress.jsonl, opencode.json. Attempts to read the parent round directory and running.json were refused (permission.rejected, external_directory / read). No shell, no writes.
OBSERVED: I cannot inspect the 97 SID+recall pairs, the exported tables, or the Issue #126 reference artefacts. Ground truth for this proposal is therefore only the prompt text: the 97-pair scoreboard, the HBAA result at +0.701 (history barycentre of source reps, mean over ten negatives, temperature reduction), the failed partition-geometry family (covering radius -0.146, adj R2 +0.156, margin -0.081, softmax path -0.488, cell expected rank +0.30, cell rank lift +0.34).
REASONING: the scoreboard says the only surviving signal is the frozen reference used as a CONTRAST (positive vs negatives); every metric built from the partition alone dies, and every likelihood-like metric must be null-corrected because it otherwise rewards collapse (softmax path's -0.49 tracks -0.78 with level-2 bucket count). So the admissible design space is: (reference contrast) x (query aggregation) x (negative summarisation) x (chance correction). HBAA occupies barycentre-query x mean-of-ten-negatives x no null. Untouched cells of that grid: the per-pair query mixture (instead of a per-item barycentre) and the target-side representation (instead of the source side), combined with an analytic size-matched null instead of no null.
OPEN: whether s_i and t_i share one ball cannot be verified from here, so the proposal must state that failure mode explicitly.

STAGE 2 - the one novel ingredient: a size-biased rank null inside the ball, and why it is the missing piece.
GOAL: pick a reduction that is not HBAA, not expected rank (already +0.30), and not likelihood (already -0.49).
READ: prompt scoreboard only.
OBSERVED / DERIVED: let cells c carry mass w_c and let the query pick a positive cell; define p(c) = sum of w over cells at least as far as c, and p+ = p(c(b)). Two exact null facts I checked by hand: (i) if the positive cell is drawn size-biased and independently of geometry, E[p] = 0.5*(1 - sum_c w_c^2) and E[obs surprisal] = E[null surprisal] = -sum_c w_c log p(c), so the gain e = -log p+ + sum_c w_c log p(c) has mean exactly 0 for ANY code-blind table of any size; (ii) a one-code table gives p = 1 and p(c) = 1, so e = 0 exactly, not a large negative and never a reward. Therefore the size-biased null removes the collapse and the many-cells biases that killed hyp_hsoftmax_path, without a tuned correction term.
REASONING: combine that null with the two unused axes. Query = each distinct TRAIN pair (a,b) separately (the finest version of "the whole training history", which a barycentre only coarsens and makes multi-modal histories wrong); candidate cell representative = Frechet barycentre in the ball of the TARGET-side reps of the cell members (target side is unused by HBAA, which uses source-side means); geometry = Poincare ball of curvature -K with K = 1/tau^2 from the frozen temperature, so no free constant.
OPEN: numerical guard at the ball boundary and the level-1 blindness, both to be stated in RISKS / FAILURE MODE.

STAGE 3 - COMPLETE ANSWER (final record, condensed; full block printed in the reply).
METRIC: hyp_succ_nullgain_l1
TITLE: Null-corrected hyperbolic surprisal of the true successor's level-1 cell.
FORMULA: K = 1/tau^2 (tau = frozen reference temperature); ball radius 1/sqrt K. phi_s(x) = (1/sqrt K) tanh((sqrt K/2)||x||/sigma_s) x/||x||, sigma_s = TRAIN median norm; phi_t likewise. d_H(u,v) = (1/sqrt K) arcosh(1 + 2K||u-v||^2/((1-K||u||^2)(1-K||v||^2))). mu_c = hyperbolic Frechet barycentre (Karcher, medoid init, 32 iterations, Mobius log/exp) of {phi_t(t_i) : i in cell c, TRAIN}. w_c = TRAIN cell mass / total. For each distinct TRAIN pair (a,b): q = phi_s(s_a), d_c = d_H(q, mu_c), p(c) = sum of w over cells with d >= d_c, p+ = p(L1(b)). e(a,b) = -log p+ + sum_c w_c log p(c). SCORE = mean over pairs, 0 if K1 = 1 or no pairs.
INPUTS: SID level-1 codes; frozen reference s_i, t_i, tau; TRAIN pairs only.
GEOMETRY: curvature -1/tau^2 entering via the tanh ball map, the arcosh Poincare distance, the Mobius Karcher barycentre, and the distance ordering used for the rank.
WHY: Stage 3 recall@10 is decided by how much candidate mass the true successor's level-1 code removes for a real query, in the reference's geometry - that is p+ and its excess over chance. Unlike Q_H it reads the reference, so tables with equal level-1 occupancy but different placement separate; unlike HBAA it keeps every pair as its own query (no history barycentre, which is lossy for multi-modal histories), uses the full negative CDF instead of a mean of ten, and uses the target side. The size-biased null is the piece the failed likelihood lacked: derivable facts checked by hand - for a code-blind table E[p] = 0.5(1 - sum w^2) and E[e] = 0 exactly, and a one-code table gives e = 0, so collapse and shattering are neutralised analytically, not by a tuned penalty (softmax path failed at -0.49 because it tracked bucket count at -0.78).
COMPUTE: m x K1 x d = 3e9 flops for m <= 2e5, K1 <= 256, d = 64 -> about 10-20 s numpy; barycentres 5e7 flops; well under a minute.
RISKS: requires one shared ball for s and t; boundary guard 1-K||u||^2 >= 1e-12; popularity confound; conservative >= tie rule.
FAILURE MODE: one-code table gives exactly 0 (floor), and any size-preserving random relabelling gives 0; blind below level 1, so a good root partition with randomised deeper levels scores as if good (level 2+ is near item-identifier, Q_H 2 = +0.287, 3 = +0.393).
END METRIC
